resolution: Found why the batch fix didn't dent the 900ms: transactions were never the dominant cost. Seq allocation reads MAX(seq) on EVERY append and the events table had NO index on seq — a full table scan per append. Measured on the user's live DBs: world log = 27,508 rows, sessions log = 33,832 rows; a 358-event move does 716 appends = 716 scans of ~30k rows each, which IS the ~900ms. Fix (595e3a9ce): CREATE INDEX events_seq — the MAX read measured sub-millisecond on the live world DB afterward. Also delivered the full story the user asked for: commitMany's [PLACEFREEZE] line now prints channelMs/markerMs plus a per-append breakdown (seqMs/jsonMs/insertMs/foldMs via the data layer's new appendProbe), so any future stall names its component instead of one opaque totalMs. game verify GREEN 72/72. Next move of that building should print a commitMany line in the tens of ms with the breakdown visible — if foldMs dominates what's left, the per-event O(N) pieces-array fold is the next target.
